title: Knowledge check: Reusable Utilities and Shared Middleware

questions.prompt: In Reusable Utilities and Shared Middleware, which statement best describes Common validation functions?
options: Define required, optional and rejected values explicitly, validate types and constraints, and return a consistent client error before the data reaches business logic.
Normalize expected failures into safe, predictable responses and forward unexpected failures to the final error handler. Keep diagnostic details in protected logs, not public responses.
Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
questions.answer_key: Define required, optional and rejected values explicitly, validate types and constraints, and return a consistent client error before the data reaches business logic.
questions.explanation: Define required, optional and rejected values explicitly, validate types and constraints, and return a consistent client error before the data reaches business logic.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Reusable Utilities and Shared Middleware?
options: Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.
Separate HTTP handling from business rules, persistence, and integration clients. Dependency injection and consistent contracts make modules easier to test; avoid abstractions that hide control flow.
questions.answer_key: Separate HTTP handling from business rules, persistence, and integration clients. Dependency injection and consistent contracts make modules easier to test; avoid abstractions that hide control flow.
questions.explanation: Separate HTTP handling from business rules, persistence, and integration clients. Dependency injection and consistent contracts make modules easier to test; avoid abstractions that hide control flow.

questions.prompt: A change related to Reusable Utilities and Shared Middleware appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
